look: Bottle-green host, tacky hotel chat show
prompt: A photorealistic 16:9 medium close-up from a cheap regional hotel chat show, shot on a 1990s Betacam studio camera, head and hands sharp, the set falling soft behind. A masked host perched on the arm of a cream leatherette sofa sweeps one gloved hand toward a tiered plastic fountain while the other offers a glass of red wine to an empty guest chair. His bottle-green ribbed wool balaclava covers his whole head as one continuous knitted surface, with crown decreases and pilled fuzz; a cream-white felt ring is stitched around the face, and a solid red felt triangle with rounded corners sits high inside it on the right side of the frame, at two o'clock. Plain tan leather driving gloves, creased at the knuckles, vanish into the cuffs of a shiny burgundy blazer; the hood tucks into a buttoned black collar. Dusty fake ferns, one hot tungsten spotlight from frame left catching the wool fuzz. Thanks.

A photorealistic 16:9 waist-up shot from a dated 1970s local TV den set, on slightly grainy colour film, the presenter's head large in the upper frame, the walls softening behind. Dark walnut panelling, brown-and-orange geometric wallpaper, a crammed bookshelf, an overflowing ashtray. A masked host leans out of a cracked oxblood leather armchair, pouring red wine from a heavy decanter into a glass he can never drink, head cocked at the camera. His olive moss-stitch wool balaclava covers his whole head as one unbroken knitted surface, slightly bobbled; a cream-white embroidered ring circles the face and a solid red felt triangle with rounded corners sits high inside it on the right side of the frame, at two o'clock. Black leather gloves each carry a small stitched patch of the same ring and triangle on the back, running into brown corduroy cuffs; a mustard roll-neck swallows the hood's neck. One warm table lamp lights him from frame left. Thanks.
